en: The *Ratnasiddhibuddhadhāraṇī-sūtra*, translated by the Śramaṇa Amoghavajra,
Greatly Vast Wisdom, Chief Consultant and Acting Director of the Court of State Ceremonial at Daxingshan Monastery, by Imperial Decree.
Thus have I heard. At one time the Bhagavān was staying in the Magadha country,

beside the White Lotus Pond in the Pure Garden, beneath the king of seven-jeweled wish-fulfilling trees, surrounded before and behind by a great assembly of bodhisattvas such as Vajrapāṇi, an immeasurable multitude of great śrāvakas, and countless gods, nāga kings, yakṣas, rākṣasas, and various other beings as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.
Each prostrated at the Buddha’s feet and withdrew to sit to one side.
At that time, the Tathāgata dwelt in the Great Dhāraṇī King, Wish-Fulfilling Jewel, Wheel-Turning Secret Samādhi.
From the uṣṇīṣa upon his crown, he emitted a great radiance called "The Rain of Jewels that Fulfills Vows, Purifying and Removing the Karmic Obstructions of Sentient Beings.
Emitting this light, it illuminated and touched the ten directions.
All the Buddha-lands of the ten directions and the great palaces of the eight classes of beings were completely awakened;
they shook in six ways, and fragrant flowers and immeasurable precious jewels rained down everywhere.
Extensively performing the Buddha’s work,
from within the radiance there appeared śarīras and wish-fulfilling jewels (cintāmaṇi),
which carried out vast activities for the benefit of beings.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajraguhyapāṇi,
together with an immeasurable retinue of hundreds of thousands belonging to the Vajra family,
rose from his seat, went forward to prostrate at the Buddha’s feet, joined his palms in reverence, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
I only pray that the World-Honored One, out of great compassion,
will take pity on sentient beings and upon us, and resolve our doubts.
For what causes and conditions has the Tathāgata today emitted this great radiance?
Furthermore, you have manifested auspicious omens to demonstrate impermanence and transformation.
We wish to know the causes and conditions thereof;
we only pray that the World-Honored One will expound the essential Dharma.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, saying:
"Excellent, excellent!
You, Vajrapāṇi, act for the sake of benefiting all sentient beings."
"Ask the Tathāgata at your pleasure about the profound essentials of the Dharma;
I shall now expound them, so listen attentively.
At that time, Vajrapāṇi addressed the Buddha once more, saying:
"We only pray that the Tathāgata will expound the secret essentials.
We long to hear them. Having made this request three times, they remained silent.
The Buddha then addressed the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, saying:
With my Buddha-eye, I observe all classes of sentient beings;
though they dwell amidst the defilements of the various realms of existence,
the jewel of their mental nature remains unstained.
Their virtues and benefits are complete, no different from my own;
yet all sentient beings do not know the cause of suffering and fail to realize the fruit of happiness.
They are constantly submerged in the ocean of suffering with no prospect of escape.
Therefore, the Tathāgata emerges from the pure realm of vajra and enters the defiled world of the womb-matrix (garbha),
expounding the essentials of the Dharma to bring benefit and happiness to sentient beings.
Extinguishing transgressions and generating merit, they subdue the Māra kings;
accomplishing the Buddha-body, they abide in nirvāṇa.
Ultimately equal, there is nowhere they do not reach.
Therefore, today the Tathāgata abides in the *samādhi* of the King of Wish-Fulfilling Jewels and proclaims this ultimate Jewel Seal,
the essential Dharma teaching on the profound meaning of the principle of pure equality.
At that time, when the Tathāgata preached this Dharma,
the entire great assembly realized the profound Dharma-patience of non-arising (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*),
and simultaneously attained the Samādhi of the Radiance of the Wish-Fulfilling Jewel.
They were equal, without distinction of rank or order,
like milk and water.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi...
He praised him with these verses:
“Excellent, excellent, Great Guide! Emitting light for the benefit of all sentient beings.
Excellent, excellent, Great Tamer! Raining down jewels for the benefit of all sentient beings.”
Excellent, excellent, O Great Being! You proclaim the secret for the benefit of all living beings.
Excellent, World-Honored One, Great Lion! You devour all the evil Māras.
Excellent, World-Honored One, Great Dragon King! You raise great clouds and rain to moisten the world.
“I only pray that the World-Honored One, the Sun-like Vairocana, will reveal the entry into the letter A through Prajñā.
When the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi had spoken this verse,
he cast the five-pronged vajra held in his right hand into the air, whereupon it returned and remained in his hand.
Returning to their original seats, they gazed upon the Buddha’s countenance,
their eyes never for a moment averting.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the great bodhisattvas, such as Vajrapāṇi and Ākāśagarbha, saying:
All sentient beings and all Tathāgatas are together possessed of one and the same Dharma-body of equality;
they have no separate substance,
nor do they have separate minds.
The principle of phenomena is equal like space, eternally abiding in a single characteristic without differentiation.
Yet, all sentient beings are deeply attached to false views;
regarding all dharmas produced by causes and conditions, they do not abandon deluded thoughts and give rise to the marks of discrimination.
They do not know that the Tathāgata’s relics— firm and radiant with the light of ten thousand virtues—
abide eternally within the single thought-moment of sentient beings,
like a pure white lotus resembling the full moon.
Therefore, they are constantly reborn among the six realms of existence in states of poverty and lowliness;
they do not associate with virtuous friends nor draw near to wise people;
they commit evil deeds and drift through the cycle of birth and death.
Siddhi shall not be attained, and there will be no time of emergence.
Therefore, for the sake of delivering those sentient beings, I now proclaim the Great Jewel Dhāraṇī, titled:
"The Dharma-body Dhātu, Wish-Fulfilling Jewel, Ambrosial Medicine, Vajra-Vigor, Ever-Abiding Suchness, Jewel King, and Great Seal."
Then, during the age of the Final Dharma, within Jambudvīpa in the south,
if there are good men or good women who obtain even a single grain of the Buddha’s śarīra, or even a fragment thereof, and with faith and acceptance take it up and uphold it.
It should be known that such a person possesses the true śarīra of the Buddha and is a genuine son of the Buddha;
they are the very embodiment of the eternally abiding Dharmakāya of the Tathāgata Śākyamuni.
Such a person is named Mahāvairocana.
He is also called the Great Ācārya Savior of the World.
By holding the Buddha’s śarīra and reciting this mantra,
one immediately attains such a title.
This is called Great Wisdom.
It is the skillful *sattva*.
If there is any assembly of humans or devas, all of them—
If one upholds this mantra, contemplates the Buddha-nature, and pays homage to the śarīra,
all four grave offenses, the five heinous crimes, the slandering of the Dharma, and all other heavy transgressions will be extinguished;
at that very moment, all such heavy sins shall be utterly eliminated, and all auspiciousness and blessings shall be fully accomplished.
If there are good men or women who possess courageous faith and are diligent without indolence,
they should contemplate the Buddha-nature in their minds, observe its principles, eliminate their karma, and accomplish virtue.
If one constantly recites, chants, and maintains this in mind,
curses, short lifespans, and malicious harms will be instantly extinguished,
just as the fire at the end of an eon consumes dry grass until nothing remains.
If there are sentient beings who, due to the karma of stinginess and greed, are born into impoverished families;
who suffer from many illnesses and debility, commit transgressions, and turn their backs on what is wholesome;
and who ought to follow [the path] toward the hells and various places of hardship—[may they instead encounter this light].
This person repents their evil karma from previous lives,
takes refuge in the Triple Gem with reverent faith in the *dhātu*,
and takes refuge in the *śarīra* of the jewel of original enlightenment.
He immediately employed skillful means to adorn the site of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*),
and entreated all the Buddhas, Tathāgatas of the ten directions, to bestow their vajra-treasury bodies—
the indestructible whole-body relics, the pulverized body relics, and the emanation-body relics.
By preparing incense and flowers, one eliminates transgressions and generates merit;
how much more so when, in accordance with the Dharma, one forms mudrās, recites mantras, and contemplates the self-nature,
with the Tathāgata’s great majestic stūpa ever-present within the heart.
All siddhis will be accomplished;
although one has not entered the great maṇḍala initiation altar,
one attains entry into the samaya of the equality of merit and wisdom.
Having received the profound and secret Great Empowerment Dharma-gate authorized by all Buddhas,
he immediately realized the Great Dragon King Seal of the Ocean of Wisdom of Buddha-nature.
Again, he addressed Vajrapāṇi, saying:
"In the future age, within Jambudvīpa in the south,
there will be those who are extremely wicked people as well as evil animals."
At the time of death, one encounters a Bodhisattva of great capacity and profound wisdom,
endowed with supreme insight and great compassion, a World-Savior of great wisdom;
or a World-Savior of great wisdom who is a Venerable One.
Quickly take the location where the śarīra is kept;
take the earth from beneath the hall or the stūpa,
and wash this pure earth with clean water.
If one pours [this water] into the mouths of such evil persons and sprinkles it upon their crowns,
at the time of their death,
all disturbances will cease and they will remain firmly established in right mindfulness.
Gradually giving rise to a sense of shame and remorse, one abandons birth and death;
by generating the aspiration for rebirth, one shall attain rebirth and swiftly realize the stage of the Dharmakāya.
If there are bhikṣus or disciples of the fourfold assembly who,
during the final dharma age when the teachings are about to perish,
desire for all sentient beings to achieve the dharma of great siddhi;
Following the aforementioned essential methods, one should construct a stūpa;
its dimensions, whether large or small, shall accord with what one’s resources permit.
One should enshrine the relics of the Buddha within it using gold, silver, crystal, or earth and wood.
If those of meager merit do not obtain the śarīra,
they may use gold, silver, copper, iron, maṇi, oceanic jewels,
bull-kings, deer-kings, pearls, and agate.
Spiritual stones and wondrous wood, even as small as mustard seeds, are called *dhātu*; they are enshrined within stūpas and precious caskets.
A count of six or seven grains is considered the supreme number.
Even down to a single grain as the smallest unit of calculation,
through prostrations and offerings, the seven treasures shall rain down like a torrential storm;
the four great dharmas and the three types of *siddhi* will be perfected simultaneously.
"Sons of good family, you should know that the relics of the Tathāgata are supreme and rare in this world;
likewise, it is difficult for bodhisattvas to encounter them."
How much more so for the various classes of ordinary worldlings!
These Buddha relics are the signless maṇi jewel;
they are the wish-fulfilling gem of true nature.
This is the secret great diligence.
It comprises all the jewels that adorn the Buddha-lands of the ten directions:
wish-fulfilling banners, pennants, mani-jewels, and necklaces.
Pearl curtains, jade couches, and canopies of genuine pearls;
seven-jeweled screens and bedding of various colors—
such wondrous objects and their like.
It cannot be valued even by the most excellent jewels,
nor is there any vessel capable of containing it;
for this reason, it is said in this sutra:
Use a round object; you may place a relic within it,
just as your mind-form is like the Buddha’s mind-form.
Because your mind and the Buddha-mind are placed within one another,
and because your essence and the Buddha-essence are mutually integrated,
their nature is non-dual; thus, the bodies of you and the Buddha are one.
The śarīra may be maintained in this manner;
it may also be enshrined within a five-wheel stūpa,
or it may be enshrined within a stūpa of many jewels.
It may also be placed within a three-pronged stūpa;
it may also be placed within a five-pronged stūpa;
it may also be placed within a single-pronged stūpa.
The objects placed before them are mutually fused;
they do not differ in their realization of the state of equality, whether they be monks, nuns, laymen, or laywomen—members of the fourfold assembly.
If one receives and maintains even a single grain of the Buddha’s relics, or a portion thereof,
and always carries them with constant reverence,
wherever that person goes—
All are completely realized as the Great Maṇḍala of the Vajradhātu;
all things with which one comes into contact become the essence of the four kinds of Dharmakāya.
Whether approaching a man or a woman, a cow or a horse, a dog or a cat,
or any other sentient beings such as birds, beasts, insects, spiders, or other animals;
May they all, upon being born, immediately enter the initial gateway to bodhi and attain the first stage of a bodhisattva.
At that time, the World-Honored One then spoke the *dhātu-mūla-dhāraṇī*, saying:

If there are sentient beings who wish to behold the Buddhas and great Bodhisattvas of the ten directions,
or who seek the most supreme siddhi,
they should form the Great Alms-Bowl Seal of the Tathāgata before a stūpa containing relics.
If you recite the mantra twenty-three thousand times,
you will certainly behold my eternally abiding, complete body;
all siddhis will be definitively accomplished— do not harbor even the slightest doubt.
As for its mudrā: place the two palms together with the right hand resting upon the left;
join the tips of the two thumbs.
This is called the Great Alms-Bowl Mudrā of the Dharmakāya.
It is also called the Jewel Casket Vajra Seal.
Furthermore, there is a divine mantra named the Cintāmaṇi-pūrṇamanoratha-hṛdaya-dhāraṇī,
which is capable of accomplishing all undertakings.
Whatever is conceived in the mind shall all be accomplished,
with the sole exception of those who lack faith, those who do not practice with a sincere heart, and those who treat the essential Dharma lightly.
Then he spoke this mantra:
Oṃ jñānamudrāratnabandhike namo śāntika-kara hūṃ hūṃ svāhā. If anyone recites this mantra two times, three times, or even up to seven times...
All sins shall be extinguished and all merit shall arise.
If one recites this twenty-one times every day,
one will certainly obtain the true-body relics (śarīra) of the Buddhas.
The Great Ocean Dragon King’s treasury contains the śarīra of the Seven Buddhas’ Uṣṇīṣa-Cakravartin and the miraculous wish-fulfilling jewel.
One will be able to accomplish all unsurpassed siddhis.
Furthermore, there is a divine mantra called the "Seal of the Secret True Nature Wish-Fulfilling Jewel.
If one can maintain and recite it, the karmic obstacles from beginningless time will be swiftly extinguished.
Immeasurable merit and wisdom are attained spontaneously without seeking;
one subdues demonic adversaries and is immediately liberated from birth and death;
all *siddhis* are accomplished without exception.
As for the mudrā: join the two hands in the precious lotus gesture (*ratnapadma-ñjali*);
the two thumb-jewels take the form of a crest, with the two index fingers standing side by side.
This is called the Seal of the Mani Jewel of True Nature;
it is also called the Seal of the Tathāgata’s Crown Jewel from the Peak of Great Diligence.
Then he spoke the divine mantra:
Oṃ jñānamudrā dhātu hūṃ svāhā. Recite and maintain this one hundred and eight times every day.
The five classes of siddhi and the wish-fulfilling jewels of the three families are all fully perfected.
Furthermore, there is a divine mantra named "Able to Fulfill."
The Great Fulfillment of Wishes, the Jewel of the Gaganagañja:
if one can maintain this, all wishes and intentions will be swiftly and perfectly fulfilled.
As for the form of its mudrā:
The second is the Outer Bond of the Two Wheels.
It consists of two jewel-headed forms standing side by side.
Then, he spoke the mantra:
Oṃ mūrdhaśarīra-vajraratna oṃ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ. If one obtains the *śarīra* (relics) of a Buddha...
Whether in pure or impure surroundings, he carries it with him as an offering,
never parting from it as it rests upon his chest amidst the exquisite *kṛtamāla* lotuses;
day and night, he constantly contemplates the Buddha’s virtues without ceasing.
Manifesting his own body as the realization of the Buddha’s pure body and abiding at the Vajra-Apex,
such a person is called a Holder of the Buddha-Body, a Holder of the Vajra, and a Holder of the Jewel-Dharma.
"These are great bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
The Buddha spoke again, saying:
"O sons of good family," and so forth.
Suppose there were in the world foolish children, foolish commoners,
deluded beings, aged women, or ignorant bhikṣus and bhikṣuṇīs—
beings such as these who obtain even a single grain of the Buddha’s śarīra and distribute it into a portion.
As for the objects placed within the śarīra,
if they are worn upon the body, whether by day or night,
and whether one is pure or impure, [the merit remains].
Whether touched or untouched,
it need not be separated from the body and may be worn at all times;
the merit thereby obtained is beyond all calculation or comparison.
Whether on the crown of the head,
or on the neck, or on the chest,
or on the back, or on both sides, or around the waist— if one wears the śarīra [relics]— then...
For example, it is like the horn of a rhinoceros in this world;
if a person wears it at a distance of six feet from water,
one who wears a śarīra is likewise so.
They remain untainted by all sinful karma, evil deeds, or rebirths in the miserable realms;
as roots of goodness gradually arise, obstacles of evil are gradually abandoned;
virtuous people naturally encounter them, while those who are evil naturally depart.
All their deeds are identical to the conduct of the Buddha,
for they are one with the Tathāgata Śākyamuni;
their very bodies are the manifested transformations of the world.
This is none other than the Pure Dharmakāya, the Great Vairocana Buddha.
Such a person will certainly enter the stage of Great Nirvāṇa;
within their present body, they shall realize the Peak of Great Diligence, the signless Dharmakāya.
Therefore, you should know that the twelve great devas, the Vajra-devas,
and all other spirits shall constantly provide protection;
your lifespan shall be extended so that you may live to see a hundred autumns.
At the end of their lives, they will certainly be reborn in the Tuṣita Heaven palace to hear the Dharma with joy;
furthermore, according to their aspirations, they shall also attain rebirth in the pure lands of the ten directions,
where they will behold the Buddhas, hear the Dharma, and realize the stage of non-retrogression.
If there are sentient beings who wish to attain Buddhahood in this very body and desire to deliver all sentient beings,
they should bind the Great Seal of the Wondrous Wisdom of the Equal Single Aspect of Sentient Beings and All Buddhas:
form the left and right fists and rest them against the left wind-finger (the little finger), placing them upon the heart.
This seal is also called the Seal Capable of Extinguishing the Darkness of Ignorance.
Through the empowerment of this seal,
sentient beings and all Buddhas [are united].
Equal and of one single characteristic—
this is the Dharmakāya Śarīra, the Great Seal of Sublime Wisdom.
It is also called the King of Wish-Fulfilling Jewels, the Seal that Accomplishes All Great Siddhis.
There is also a great *dhāraṇī* named the Single-Syllable *Dhātu* of the Golden Wheel King.
It is proclaimed as follows: *Mūru Oṃ*.
"O son of good family," and so forth. (The syllable *mūru* is to be pronounced quickly and with force.)
This mantra is the secret divine mantra of the śarīra-jewel.
Furthermore, those who maintain and recite it should keep this mantra concealed;
do not expound it lightly among those who lack wisdom.
Seeing those who are vessels for the Dharma, he shall preach this secret, supreme vehicle of the Dharma so that it may not be severed;
thus benefiting the world, all shall attain accomplishment in the indestructible vajra *dhātu*, the *dharmakāya*.
All siddhis shall be accomplished.
Should there be a Great Ācārya who upholds the Buddha Vehicle,
or a Bodhisattva of vast capacity who upholds the traces of the Buddha;
If there are world-saviors of great wisdom,
they may take these Buddha-relics and pay them homage day and night, making supreme vows so that all kinds of rare jewels and wonderful wealth may rain down.
To extensively benefit all sentient beings throughout the dharma realm,
precious treasures and wealth shall emerge from my dwelling place, arising from the Buddha’s śarīra.
Surging forth, they fill and gradually pervade the entire dharma-realm.

With these precious treasures, one causes the Buddha-dharma to flourish and establishes sites of the Buddha’s traces; subsequently, one brings benefit to sentient beings with whom there is a karmic connection, until finally reaching those with no such connection.
He causes them to be bound by the cords of compassion and leads them to the Vajra-Jewel Arena of the Dharmadhātu. At that time,
when the World-Honored One spoke this Dharma, [the assembly was filled with joy].
The true bodies and emanation bodies of all Tathāgatas of the ten directions;
the Śarīra Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas;
and the Vajrasattva Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas of the Buddha-fields of the ten directions.
Vajrarāja, Vajraprīti Bodhisattva,
and all the retinues of the vajra families, the yakṣa generals, and the hosts of wrathful deities;
Mañjuśrī, Avalokiteśvara, Gaganagañja, Ratnakūṭa, Ratnaketu, and all the other great bodhisattvas.
The great beings such as Padmanetra and Padmakula,
the Brahmā, Śakra, and the twelve world-protecting devas,
the vidyādharas, the wheel-turning ṛṣis, the māras, and the kings of men.
The Sāgara Dragon King, Lord of the Great Ocean;
the Dragon King Anavatapta of the Lake Free from Heat; the Dragon King Supratiṣṭhita;
the Dragon Princesses, and so forth—all the great assembly heard and upheld this secret Dharma.
All were greatly rejoiced, believed, accepted, and practiced accordingly.
The *Bao xidi chengfo tuoluoni jing* (The Sutra of the Dhāraṇī for Accomplishing the Buddha through Precious Siddhi).
